security_audit.summary: All 17 static findings are false positives: backticks mark inline code, URLs reference relevant public documentation, and token symbols are not reconnaissance. The skill still presents contextual risks because it relies on mutable remote documentation and can generate workflows that trade real assets through configured accounts. Publication should require transaction confirmation and remote-content safeguards.

remediation.issue: Generated workflows can submit real token swaps through configured Ape accounts.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval before signing or broadcasting. Show the network, token addresses, amounts, route, slippage, fees, recipient, and minimum output.

remediation.issue: The required documentation sources use mutable branches and stable channels.
remediation.suggestion: Pin vetted versions where possible. Treat fetched content as untrusted data, restrict domains, and ignore instructions embedded in remote pages.

content.user_title: Build Safer Uniswap Workflows with Ape
content.value_statement: Uniswap integration requires current SDK knowledge and careful transaction planning. This skill guides Ape-based pricing, routing, swaps, and Silverback automation with practical safeguards.
actual_capabilities: Fetches current public documentation for uniswap-sdk, Ape, and ape-tokens before proposing an implementation.
Collects the target network, token pair, and intended action before designing a workflow.
Guides pair indexing with uni.index or uni.install for standard and Silverback environments.
Explains price queries, route searches, token swaps, and liquid intermediate token selection.
Supports Silverback bot integration with live indexing and in-memory market state.
Recommends quote review and small initial swaps for higher-risk transactions.
limitations: Requires Python, Ape, a configured account for live trades, an installed tokenlist, and network access for documentation.
Does not guarantee prices, route quality, liquidity, transaction inclusion, or swap outcomes.
Does not remove smart contract, slippage, MEV, token, provider, or private key risks.
Guidance depends on current documentation, supported deployments, provider configuration, and accurate user input.

use_cases.title: Prototype read-only market queries
use_cases.description: Plan Ape scripts that index pairs, query prices, and compare routes without creating transactions.

use_cases.title: Prepare a reviewed token swap
use_cases.description: Build a guarded swap workflow that presents route, quote, slippage, fees, and minimum output before approval.

use_cases.title: Design Silverback automation
use_cases.description: Integrate live Uniswap indexing and route selection into a monitored bot with explicit transaction controls.

prompt_templates.title: Review prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Uniswap setup for [network]. List the required Python, Ape, account, tokenlist, and documentation prerequisites. Do not create a transaction.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a price query
prompt_templates.prompt: Using current official documentation, plan a read-only price query for [token A] and [token B] on [network]. Explain pair indexing and route assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a guarded swap
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare an Ape workflow to swap [amount] of [token A] for [token B] on [network]. Quote first and stop before broadcasting. Show token addresses, route, slippage, fees, recipient, and minimum output for approval.

prompt_templates.title: Design Silverback automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Silverback bot for [strategy] on [network] using uniswap-sdk. Include indexing, route selection, simulations, limits, monitoring, failure handling, and manual emergency controls. Never sign or broadcast without explicit authorization.

output_examples.input: Compare routes for swapping 1 WETH to USDC on Ethereum without executing a trade.
output: Checks that WETH and USDC pairs are indexed.
Compares direct and liquid intermediate routes.
Reports the quote, estimated fees, and assumptions.

output_examples.input: Prepare a guarded USDC to WETH swap on Arbitrum.
output: Confirms the network and token contract addresses.
Presents the amount, route, slippage, fees, recipient, and minimum output.
Recommends a simulation and small initial trade.
Requests approval before signing or broadcasting.

output_examples.input: Outline a Silverback bot that monitors Uniswap routes.
output: Defines pair indexing and live event tracking.
Separates read-only signals from transaction execution.
Adds exposure limits, monitoring, failure handling, and emergency controls.
Requires explicit authorization for every transaction policy.

best_practices: Verify current SDK documentation, package versions, network deployments, and token addresses before implementation.
Present the complete transaction summary and require explicit approval immediately before signing or broadcasting.
Simulate first, set conservative slippage limits, and use a small initial swap for new routes.
anti_patterns: Do not trust token symbols alone; verify chain-specific contract addresses and decimals.
Do not broadcast from a configured account without a fresh quote and explicit user approval.
Do not copy instructions from fetched pages without treating remote content as untrusted.

faq.question: Does this skill execute Uniswap trades?
faq.answer: It can guide code that executes swaps, but every signing or broadcast step should require explicit user approval.

faq.question: Which networks are supported?
faq.answer: Support depends on Ape, uniswap-sdk, provider configuration, tokenlists, and current Uniswap deployments.

faq.question: Is an Ape account required?
faq.answer: Read-only queries may not require one. Live trades require a configured account with carefully protected signing credentials.

faq.question: Why does the skill fetch documentation?
faq.answer: The SDK and Ape interfaces can change. Current documentation reduces outdated code, but fetched content must remain untrusted.

faq.question: Does the skill guarantee the best route?
faq.answer: No. Liquidity, fees, market movement, indexing state, and network conditions can change the result.

faq.question: Can it help build a Silverback bot?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide indexing, route selection, monitoring, and controls for a Silverback integration.
